title: Numerical foundations — original editorial review pack

questions.prompt: A box contains 80 blank study cards. Three-eighths are assigned to a vocabulary activity. How many cards are assigned to that activity?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/fractions.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Compute 80 × 3/8 = 10 × 3 = 30 cards. Checking 30/80 gives 3/8, so the selected share matches the stated fraction.

questions.prompt: Which fraction in simplest form is equal to the decimal 0.45?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/fractions.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Write 0.45 as 45/100. Dividing numerator and denominator by 5 gives 9/20; 9 and 20 have no common factor greater than 1.

questions.prompt: A printing job costs ₱600 before a 12% discount. There are no other charges. What is the amount paid after the discount?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/fractions.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The discount is ₱600 × 0.12 = ₱72. Subtracting it gives ₱600 − ₱72 = ₱528. Alternatively, 88% of ₱600 is ₱528.

questions.prompt: A reading target rises from 120 pages to 150 pages. What is the percentage increase relative to the original target?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/fractions.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The increase is 150 − 120 = 30 pages. Divide by the original 120 pages: 30/120 = 0.25, or a 25% increase.

questions.prompt: A learner completes 1/4 of a project on Monday and another 2/5 of the same project on Tuesday. The portions do not overlap. What fraction is completed in total?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/fractions.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Use denominator 20: 1/4 = 5/20 and 2/5 = 8/20. The nonoverlapping portions total 5/20 + 8/20 = 13/20 of the project.

questions.prompt: Two groups share 72 blank cards in the ratio 5:3. How many cards does the group receiving the larger share get?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/ratios.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The ratio has 5 + 3 = 8 equal parts. Each part is 72/8 = 9 cards, so the larger share is 5 × 9 = 45 cards. The other share is 27.

questions.prompt: Eight identical pens cost ₱120. At the same unit price and with no extra fees, how much do six pens cost?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/ratios.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The unit price is ₱120/8 = ₱15 per pen. Six pens cost 6 × ₱15 = ₱90. The assumption of an unchanged unit price is stated.

questions.prompt: Four learners each read 10 pages. Six other learners each read 15 pages. What is the mean number of pages read across all ten learners?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/ratios.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The total is 4 × 10 + 6 × 15 = 40 + 90 = 130 pages. Dividing by all 10 learners gives 13 pages per learner; group sizes are unequal.

questions.prompt: The ratio of red folders to blue folders is 3:5. If there are 18 red folders, how many blue folders are there?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/ratios.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Three ratio parts represent 18 red folders, so one part represents 6 folders. Five parts therefore represent 5 × 6 = 30 blue folders.

questions.prompt: Seven reading sessions have a mean duration of 12 minutes. One session lasting 18 minutes is removed from the data. What is the mean of the remaining six sessions?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/ratios.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The original total is 7 × 12 = 84 minutes. Removing 18 minutes leaves 66 minutes across 6 sessions. The new mean is 66/6 = 11 minutes.

questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence begins 6, 11, 16, 21. Under the stated arithmetic rule, what is the next term?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/sequences.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The common difference is +5 at every displayed transition. Adding 5 to the final term gives 21 + 5 = 26, under the stated arithmetic rule.

questions.prompt: A geometric sequence begins 160, 80, 40, 20. Under the stated geometric rule, what is the next term?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/sequences.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The common factor is 1/2: each term is half the preceding term. Multiplying 20 by 1/2 gives the next term, 10.

questions.prompt: Starting at 3, repeatedly add 4, then multiply by 2. The terms shown are 3, 7, 14, 18, 36. What is the next term under that rule?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/sequences.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: The displayed steps are +4, ×2, +4, ×2. The next operation returns to +4, so 36 + 4 = 40. Multiplication follows after that term.

questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence has first term 9 and common difference 3. What is its eighth term?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/sequences.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Reaching the eighth term takes 7 steps after the first term. Compute 9 + 7 × 3 = 30. Using 8 increments would incorrectly skip the first term.

questions.prompt: A geometric sequence has first term 2 and common factor 3. What is its fifth term?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/sequences.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Four multiplications lead from the first term to the fifth: 2, 6, 18, 54, 162. Equivalently, compute 2 × 3^4 = 162.

questions.prompt: A bicycle moves at a constant 16 kilometres per hour for 45 minutes without stopping. How far does it travel?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/word-problems.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Convert 45 minutes to 45/60 = 0.75 hour. Distance equals speed times time: 16 kilometres/hour × 0.75 hour = 12 kilometres.

questions.prompt: A printing service charges a fixed ₱25 fee plus ₱3 per page. A bill is exactly ₱160 with no other fees. How many pages were printed?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/word-problems.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Let p be the page count. From 25 + 3p = 160, subtract 25 to obtain 3p = 135. Then p = 45. Checking 25 + 3 × 45 gives ₱160.

questions.prompt: One machine completes a job in 6 hours and another completes the same-sized job in 3 hours. At constant independent rates, how long do they take together?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/word-problems.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Their rates are 1/6 and 1/3 job per hour. The sum is 1/2 job per hour, so one job takes 1 ÷ (1/2) = 2 hours. The jobs are assumed identical.

questions.prompt: Three identical notebooks plus a ₱15 delivery fee cost ₱150. With no other charges, what is the price of one notebook?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/word-problems.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Subtract the fixed fee before dividing: (₱150 − ₱15)/3 = ₱135/3 = ₱45 per notebook. Check: 3 × ₱45 + ₱15 = ₱150.

questions.prompt: A tank holds 18 litres. It fills at a constant rate of 3 litres per minute, with no outflow. How long does it take to fill from empty?
questions.sourceNotes: Original project teaching draft; see content/lessons/word-problems.md for the method. Independent human correctness/originality review pending. Not an actual CSC question.
questions.explanation: Time equals required volume divided by filling rate: 18 litres ÷ (3 litres/minute) = 6 minutes. The stated assumptions exclude outflow and changing rates.
